semantic_requirements.byte_size_and_raw_sha256: Use declared index columns only. Evidence candidates must be unique within each role, disjoint across byte-size/raw-SHA roles, and disjoint from every structural index column. Evaluate all present configured candidates per row in configuration order: select the first valid value, allow repeated valid aliases only when their normalized values agree, fail closed on conflicting valid aliases, and emit partial when a selected valid value coexists with an invalid alias. Byte size accepts only canonical ASCII non-negative decimal: zero is exactly 0, positive values begin with 1-9, and signs, separators, non-ASCII digits, surrounding whitespace, and leading zeros are invalid. When candidates are absent or all empty, emit unavailable; when every non-empty value is invalid, emit invalid; when valid evidence is incomplete or mixed with invalid values, emit partial; never infer from remarks.
semantic_requirements.facts_vs_judgments: Keep index/metadata counts, exploratory probe evidence, judgments, hypotheses and forbidden inference explicitly separate.
semantic_requirements.input_integrity: Before creating output directories or writing temporary/final output, reject canonical or hard-link aliasing between every final/stage/backup artifact path and the index, config, contract, probe, any existing referenced metadata input, and every other artifact path; reject symlink/reparse components in the output directory. Pin one no-reparse output-directory identity before the first artifact creation. Bind every stage/backup create, write, reopen, commit/restore rename, rollback delete, and finally cleanup to that pinned directory by basename-relative operations; never rediscover a mutation target through the mutable lexical parent. Use stable Win32/NT directory handles and RootDirectory-relative operations on Windows, and O_DIRECTORY/O_NOFOLLOW dir_fd-relative operations on POSIX. A changed lexical output-directory identity must stop new commits, while rollback and cleanup remain pinned; a parent-path junction/symlink swap must cause no create, overwrite, rename, or delete in the external directory. Create same-directory stage/backup files with cryptographically random names, exclusive creation, and no-follow where the platform exposes it. Parse config, contract, probe and metadata from the same stable bytes used for their SHA-256 evidence. Gate the large index with stable identity plus SHA-256 before, between and after its two streaming passes. Fully stage and reopen both outputs, snapshot the old pair, then re-verify every input and old output at the commit point. On Windows, keep every planned-existing destination open from snapshot through commit/rollback with a mandatory FILE_SHARE_READ-only lease that denies other write/delete/replace opens; this must reject same-path and hard-link writes plus pathname replacement at the kernel boundary. Retire the exact opened old file object through its own DELETE-capable handle by RootDirectory-relative NtSetInformationFile rename to a cryptographically random private backup with ReplaceIfExists=0, then publish the staged generation with ReplaceIfExists=0. All commit and rollback renames must be no-replace: no code path may use ReplaceIfExists=1. Every Windows Nt rename must run a syscall postcondition coordinator on both normal and exceptional returns: query the exact open source handle's current basename, reopen that basename relative to the pinned directory, require the same file identity, and update StableOpenFile name/temporary plus OriginalArtifact retired/backup and committed/rollback state from that kernel fact before continuing or propagating. The coordinator itself is not an infallible oracle: retain source/target candidate names and expected identity on the exact open handle, and independently converge handle-path evidence, ordinary pinned-directory reopen evidence, and a direct RootDirectory-relative NtCreateFile plus fstat identity probe. A GetFinalPathNameByHandleW failure, ordinary identity-reopen failure, or consecutive failures across both mechanisms must still resolve the real generation through the independent probe; if all signals remain ambiguous, fail closed with machine-readable candidates/identity/errors while retaining the exact handle for rollback, recovery and cleanup re-coordination. Apply this to reservation-to-private, old-final-to-backup, stage-to-final, transaction-final-to-private-stage and backup-to-final. A wrapper or asynchronous exception after a successful syscall must never leave cached pre-rename state. Before each individual commit, also bind the complete destination generation again; an absent destination that appears, an existing destination that changes, and an already committed target that changes before the next commit all fail closed. Rollback retires the exact transaction-owned final handle to its private stage name before no-replace backup restore; if a destination appears at the restore syscall, preserve it plus the unique backup and expose rollback_incomplete/recovery_files. Before rollback may report complete, prove every planned-existing old generation is restored at final; if final is missing or the unique old generation exists only at backup, report rollback_incomplete and preserve it. Emit recovery_files and cleanup_required_paths only for paths that currently exist and still match the expected owned identity; never list a stale basename or a different generation that reused a private name. A POSIX runtime without an equivalent mandatory target-generation primitive must never fall back to path-guard-plus-replace for a planned-existing destination: reject that replacement before creating stage/backup artifacts and require a fresh output directory; fresh planned-absent outputs continue to use descriptor-relative no-replace publication. Cleanup attempts every owned temporary delete and every file close, then closes the stable directory independently; a committed generation with cleanup warnings remains explicitly committed and reports cleanup_state, cleanup_warnings and cleanup_required_paths instead of becoming an opaque failed call. Keep the two published final handles out of generic temporary cleanup and return a dictionary-compatible published-generation lease owner instead of a plain dict. commit_artifact_set, run and the CLI must consume success only while that owner still holds both mandatory leases; the CLI serializes the result under lease, then performs authoritative release before emitting success. Release duplicates two exact guardians per final, closes primary and guardian handles without an unguarded internal gap, verifies both fixed basenames before and after release, and treats wrapper-after-close, directory-close, caller-abort and serialization failures as explicit handoff/release states. A generation drift observed in the final release gap must never remain committed/clean: emit rollback_incomplete plus release_errors and release_required_paths. Re-verify every input after both commits; persistent drift triggers rollback and failure. The input integrity boundary is identity plus SHA-256 at the documented read/commit/post-commit gates rather than a kernel change journal; a writer that changes and perfectly restores an input between gates (ABA), or changes it after the successful post-commit gate, is outside this contract. Destination replacement on Windows additionally uses the mandatory lease plus exact-object retirement/no-replace protocol and does not rely on those path gates for atomicity.
semantic_requirements.index_header: Before either streaming pass consumes a data row, require a non-empty header whose column names are non-empty and globally unique under case-insensitive semantics. Reject duplicate structural, byte-size, raw-SHA or other columns before analysis. The metadata pass header must exactly equal the first-pass header.
semantic_requirements.metadata: Classify actual exported metadata as generic_header_only, custom_fields_present, unavailable or parse_error; include every safe existing referenced metadata file exactly once in the sorted provenance manifest even when strict JSON or document-shape parsing fails. Process exported rows during a second streaming index pass instead of retaining one dictionary per exported row.
semantic_requirements.probe: Treat optional probe input as sample-only evidence; overall recovery estimate must remain null.
semantic_requirements.read_errors: Parse configured Expected-vs-actual messages without treating expected bytes as a declared object byte_size. Count every unmatched message, but retain only the configured-size deterministic lowest-SHA-256 sample and configured-length previews; do not retain every unique full remark in memory.
semantic_requirements.source_groups: Classify sources through ordered configuration rules, never project-specific source counts or names in code.
